As we reported in our last _Fortnightly_ , Chinese copper prices rose following the Fed’s launch of QE3 on 13th September, following a similar pattern to other exchange-traded commodities. The SHMET spot market price peaked at RMB60,160/t on 17th September and has declined somewhat, but prices remain elevated compared to those experienced since mid-May. Traders report that the market is well supplied and that spot market activity is extremely light ahead of the national holiday next week. Consumers remain unwilling to purchase too much volume in advance, preferring to destock instead. Some difficulty in obtaining financing ahead of the holidays © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **September 2012** www.crugroup.com was also noted and is clearly why the People’s Bank of China earlier this week injected RMB 290 billion into the economy through a combination of reverse repurchase agreements (repos) and 14-day contracts. Indeed, in the last week it was reported that Shanghai Shenghua Cable, a large Chinese cablemaker, will not be increasing its copper stocks prior to next week’s national holiday, due to the recent copper price rise and to cash-flow problems caused by a high level of credit being extended to its customers. Our regular survey of market participants indicated that the spot premium for imported cathode is being quoted in a range of $40/t to $60/t, about $10/t lower than the $50/t to $70/t range that we reported two weeks ago. The premium for SXEW cathode is unchanged at $40/t, with almost no activity to report for this particular product. Reported SHFE stocks rose to 166,829 tonnes on September 21st , up from 156,401 tonnes on September 14th . Our Beijing office currently estimates that total bonded warehouse stocks amount to 675,000 tonnes, which is unchanged from our estimate in the last _Fortnightly_ . SHFE reported stocks, along with CRU’s estimate of bonded warehouse stocks in both Shanghai and Nanhai, totals 784,000 tonnes, the highest level since midMay. # Copper imports rose in August Final trade statistics for August were

released on 21st September, indicating that total cathode imports were 251,008 tonnes, down from 254,339 tonnes in July, and up 6.6% compared to a year ago. Since cathode exports fell to 1,707 tonnes, down from 12,506 tonnes in July, the net imports of cathode were actually slightly higher last month, at 249,000 tonnes. The chart to the left illustrates the net import volumes of cathode, scrap and concentrate since December 2011, which was a record high level of imports of these three forms of copper combined. Note that scrap tonnage has been calculated by assuming a 35% copper content, while concentrate import volumes have been adjusted to assume a contained copper content of 28%. China imported slightly more scrap last month, and at 153,000 tonnes, this was the largest volume since the December’s 156,000 tonnes. Perhaps the most interesting development was the jump in concentrate imports to an historical high of 194,000 tonnes last month, beating the prior high of 191,000 tonnes reported for September 2010. Copper mine production has not experienced the same levels of disruption that we have become accustomed to over the last few years, while several smelters have undergone downtime this year (both planned and unplanned) leading to a softer copper concentrates market. Spot TC/RCs have appreciated accordingly, and are now in the range of $60-65/6.0-6.5¢, and we hear from market insiders that the Chinese Smelter Purchasing Team announced on 22nd September that its members had agreed a new floor for spot terms of $65/6.5¢ (exceeding the agreed contract terms for this year of $60-$63.5 and 6-6.35 cents). In reality, the floor price is not always strictly adhered to and certain Chinese smelters, particularly smaller ones, have been known to undercut it. We also have to bear in mind that negotiations over the 2013 annual contract © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **September 2012** www.crugroup.com terms are underway, and naturally the smelters are keen to present the market to their favour. Having said that, the CSPT floor tends to be a useful guide to the state of the market balance and the buying appetite of the Chinese smelters, and given that three Chinese smelters are set for scheduled maintenance in the next few weeks, it seems a reasonable assumption that spot terms are appreciating into the high $60/6.0¢s. # Yunnan Province to stockpile metal 

As part of its mandate to ensure “growth”, Yunnan province’s regional government announced that it will stockpile 300,000 tonnes of nonferrous metals, including 20,000 tonnes of copper, 200,000 tonnes of aluminium and 50,000 tonnes of zinc.  The balance of 30,000 tonnes will be made up of minor metals. Yunnan Copper’s smelter was selected to implement the stockpiling, which will take effect this month. 

This commercial stockpiling is welcomed by the region’s producers and it will be implemented as follows: The producer uses the stock as collateral for a bank loan, for which the government pays the interest. The stockpiling price is based on the market price at the time of the loan. The ownership of the metal does not change, so the producer still owns the metal after the stockpiling ends.  This measure provides producers with access to credit, and it also supports the domestic metal price. However, there may be some downward pressure on the metal price when the metal is released from the stockpile. The Yunnan provincial government previously attempted to stockpile 150,000 tonnes of metal during the global financial crisis in 2008 and early 2009.
